items.title: 61124_Mario Bauza oral history interview
items.q: When I got Dizzy into Calloway band, he was my roommate.

ctx.x:
Okay, I would like to -- we started to talk about Gillespie, but I would like to get back into Dizzy Gillespie. You talked earlier about how you got to (inaudible) and the Cab Calloway band. But if you can just start talking about the importance of Gillespie and Afro-Cuban music and how he got involved with it.

I remember your once telling me that he was jamming with you once or twice.

Well, way before that, see. When I got Dizzy into Calloway band, he was my roommate. In the back of his mind he had -- in the back of his mind he had something to improve the way of playing, something that he figured would be a volume rhythm-wise but what he was thinking of doing harmonic-wise.

First he had a (inaudible) harmonic-wise, because the average musician, he liked what he was doing. So he had to simplify everything. He went out of key, and he played funny notes and, you know, a whole lot of crazy…
trying to play with a stick.
